name: Nominal support and recovery-workspace correction
question: Which corrected four-foot geometry preserves nominal support and creates a safe executable contact mechanism across every frozen fall?

candidates.hypothesis: The inherited rear sagittal axis convention is compatible with the authored symmetric home joint angles.
candidates.falsifiedIf: The authored home has fewer than four feet within tolerance, or any frozen resting orientation has fewer than two collision-free foot contact opportunities.

candidates.hypothesis: Mirroring the rear hip and knee axes with the rear geometry makes the home angles symmetric, while moving all hip mounts outside the torso collision envelope removes the inherited permanent attachment overlap.
candidates.falsifiedIf: The authored home still has fewer than four feet within tolerance, or any frozen resting orientation lacks two genuinely collision-free foot contact opportunities.

candidates.hypothesis: The same nominal-support and hip-clearance corrections combined with bounded roll/pitch waist articulation preserve a collision-free brace while adding a direct body reorientation mechanism.
candidates.falsifiedIf: The authored home has fewer than four feet within tolerance, or any frozen resting orientation lacks two genuinely collision-free foot contact opportunities.

dynamicProbe.switchBackIf: Any frozen resting orientation lacks a collision-free transition from body reorientation into stable four-foot support after a bounded readable-controller search.

candidates.hypothesis: A bounded over-centre abduction workspace lets the four declared feet cross the inverted torso plane and create support from a motionless back fall, while modest sagittal overtravel covers the exact front-fall boundary observed in the prior probe.
candidates.falsifiedIf: The candidate loses nominal/static support, cannot create foot support from the frozen back fall, or still cannot transition all four frozen falls into stable standing without collision or joint-limit violation.

dynamicProbe.switchBackIf: The over-centre candidate cannot create and retain four-foot support in front/back recovery, or its larger workspace introduces collision or joint-limit failures.
